bc_lower_splitsville.blurb: Lower Splitsville is the bottom end of the Splitsville crag in Murrin Park, just outside Squamish. It is a small trad wall with five routes, so it suits a short session or a warm-up before heading to the taller upper section. The grades start at an easy 5.6, add a 5.8, and then settle into three routes in the 5.10 range, which makes it a reasonable pick for climbers stepping up from moderate gear leads. Most of the routes are rated at two stars. The wall sits at a modest elevation near the valley floor. To reach it, hikers either walk down past the upper wall or take the left-hand variation at the small mossy step that skirts the bluff.

bc_slesse_creek_bouldering.blurb: Slesse Creek Bouldering is a small set of problems beside the road to Chilliwack Lake in the Fraser Valley, in the trees at the mouth of the creek. It has five problems: a long traverse, a few straight-up lines and an overhanging roof problem, ranging from easy up to the V4 to V5 range, with several in the middle at V3. The stone is solid, water-worn limestone with pockets, and the landings are soft sand. The boulders stay dry in the rain, which helps on wet coastal days, but the trees keep the spot shady and the rock can be mossy. It makes a good stop for a short bouldering session, and a limestone sport crag sits close by.

bc_lucky_charms.blurb: Lucky Charms is a single boulder inside the forest within the Pemberton Boulders, in the Sea to Sky country north of Whistler. It has five problems, all bouldering, running from V2 up to one V5, with the bulk of them in the V2 to V3 range. The boulder is the next one along the forest path after the Slug Boulder, and the surrounding trees keep it shaded for most of the day. It works as a stop on a longer circuit of the Pemberton blocks rather than a destination on its own, with a mix of moderate lines and one hard problem.

bc_the_splits.blurb: The Splits is a small boulder in the forest at the Pemberton Boulders, in the Sea to Sky region north of Whistler. It sits just past Lucky Charms along the same path. There are five problems, all at the easy end, from V0 down to V1, including a sit start and a traverse, which makes it handy for beginners or for a gentle warm-up before the harder blocks nearby. The boulder is somewhat overgrown, and the tree cover keeps it mostly shaded. Most climbers will pair it with the neighbouring boulders rather than make a trip for it alone.

bc_the_maze.blurb: The Maze is one of the zones within Cobbles Bouldering, in the Fraser Valley near Hope. Cobbles is known for steep, house-sized blocks with scoops, pockets, edges and pinches. It has five boulder problems, spread widely from an easy V0 up to a V7, with a couple in the V3 range in between. That spread gives easier problems for building up and one serious test piece.
